title: The relationship of the internal space of buildings design with human behavior
research_question: To discuss the effect of internal building design on human behavior and to understand the impact of surrounding design on people, specifically by surveying employee opinions on the importance of various environmental features in their workplaces.

participants.description: Employees (256 males, 155 females) from different sectors of government and private companies in Kuwait, across age groups: 21-30, 31-40, 41-50, 51-60.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Employees' current or ideal working environments, focusing on features like colors, biophilic elements (agriculture), gathering areas, nice views, and private areas, as queried through survey questions.

measures.construct: Importance/demand for specific environmental features in the work area (colors & agriculture, gathering area, nice view, private area)
measures.instrument: Self-report survey questions (implied percentage of agreement/demand)

findings.antecedent: Importance of colors and biophilic elements (agriculture) in work area
findings.mechanism: Age-related differences in aesthetic preferences and perceived benefits of biophilic elements.
findings.quote: the employee of age 31 – 40 were the highest response about demanding colors & agriculture

findings.antecedent: Importance of colors and biophilic elements (agriculture) in work area
findings.mechanism: Age-related differences in aesthetic preferences and perceived benefits of biophilic elements.
findings.quote: comparing to the group of age at 51-60 which has the lowest demand of that issue

findings.antecedent: Importance of a nice view in the office
findings.mechanism: Older age groups may prioritize restorative views for mental well-being and stress reduction.
findings.quote: but they have the highest demand of needing nice view in the office

findings.antecedent: Importance of a private area in the work area
findings.mechanism: The need for personal space and control over social interaction is a key aspect of privacy regulation.
findings.quote: and nearly equal to the group of age 41-50 in needing their own private area

findings.antecedent: Importance of a gathering area in the work area
findings.mechanism: The need for social interaction and collaboration in the workplace, facilitated by spatial configuration.
findings.quote: the group of age 41 -50 has the highest demand.

mechanisms: Interaction between people and the spaces they occupy (Environmental psychology / Space psychology)
Influence of architectural design on mental and psychological well-being
Modulation of attention (directed attention fatigue, mental rest)
Regulation of social interaction, privacy, territoriality, and crowding (Sociological human need)
Human response through perception, cognition, and spatial behavior
Prediction error, surprise, and expectation violation in environmental processing
implementation_implications: Designing working areas to be suitable and fulfill the diverse needs of all employees, considering age and gender.
Incorporating colors, natural light, and good ventilation in work environments.
Resource departments, designers, and architects should collaborate to shape work environments that positively impact employee well-being, culture, satisfaction, and productivity.

tables.description: Chart of employee response showing the percentage of employees by age group who find certain features important (colors & agriculture, gathering area, nice view, private area).
key_stats: Descriptive percentages of employee demand for various features by age group.

limitations: Not explicitly stated by the authors, but inherent to a descriptive survey design are limitations regarding causal inference and generalizability beyond the surveyed population.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: The presence of natural elements like specific colors and biophilic features (e.g., agriculture) in a work environment positively influences human demand and preference for that space.
